text:
Alex: Heads-up — p95 decode latency spiked ~2x in canary after the last merge, looks correlated with the pipelined KV prefetch change. Observed across short-seq and medium-seq workloads. :eyes:
Maria: where are you seeing it? dashboards or local runs?
Alex: dashboards first (per-route p95), then reproduced on a small stress harness. Canary summary from this morning attached by CI Bot below.
CI Bot: CI Canary: 2954106001 - decode-p95 regression detected on model r1.4.2-canary. p95 increased from 48ms -> 102ms for short sequences. See /ci/canary/2954106001
Sudha: hmm the pipelined prefetch introduces an extra memcpy and additional small-kernel churn when KV hits are high. Could cause SLO tail jumps if batching shrinks. Which PR was that?
Alex: PR #7821 — the one that tries to overlap KV loads with attention compute and uses the new 'pipelined_kv' kernel path.
Jordan: if this is causing thrash we should consider a quick revert or a targeted guardrail. Do we have a bisect plan?
Ryan: I can run a narrow bisect on the canary cluster — trying reverting PR #7821 locally first. If it repros away then we have a smoking gun.
Maria: Also capture a perf trace (nsys) and a small perf top for the problematic workload. Short seq reproduces faster. Alex, can you post the `perf top` snippet you mentioned?
Alex: Posting the trimmed perf sample: ```
  28.7%  libruntime.so  memcpy
  18.1%  libruntime.so  kv_prefetch_kernel_small
  12.4%  libruntime.so  attention_compute_kernel
   9.3%  libc.so        sys_write
```
Maria: memcpy jumping that high lines up with extra data movement from the pipelined path. If the batcher decided smaller batches (because of timing), the relative memcpy cost could dominate.
Sudha: Another clue: logs show increased KV cache evictions around the same spike windows. Pipelined_kv's prefetch might be touching extra slots and invalidating locality. I added a quick log snippet: ```
[2026-03-17T09:12:03Z] kv_cache: probe_hit=342, probe_miss=41, evictions=23
[2026-03-17T09:12:05Z] kv_cache: probe_hit=310, probe_miss=76, evictions=98
```
Jordan: That evictions jump is scary. Even if latency per op is similar, eviction churn increases tail latency.
CI Bot: Canary check: additional run with PR #7821 reverted shows p95 back to ~50ms (run id 2954108002).
Alex: Ryan, can you confirm with a quick seq-run that reverting PR #7821 restores latency on the same hardware config?
Ryan: Running now. Command: `./deploy_canary --image=canary-latest --override-pr=7821 --run=shortseq`
Ryan: Result: revert run p95=52ms, matching baseline. I also captured nsys timeline — reduced memcpy hotspots and fewer kernel launches.
Maria: Sounds like a revert candidate then. Any chance we can add a guard (feature flag) to only enable pipelined_kv on long-seq workloads where it helps?
Sudha: The pipelined path is beneficial for long sequences because overlapping KV loads hides attention latency. For short sequences the overhead wins. We should gate by sequence-length histogram (or batch-size). I'll draft a patch to check avg_seq_len > threshold before switching.
Jordan: For rollout plan: revert PR #7821 on canary immediately, hold the broader rollout, and schedule a follow-up PR that gates the path and adds eviction tests. Ops Bot, please hold the release pipeline for the next 3 hours.
Ops Bot: Release pipeline paused for `runtime-rollout` for 3h starting 2954110000.
Alex: Filing the incident and assigning follow-ups: - reversion PR (#7830) by Ryan - gating patch draft by Sudha - add regression test (short-seq p95) by Maria
Ryan: WIP: opened revert PR #7830 and started canary revert deploy (deploy id 2954109009).
Sudha: I'll start the gating branch now and add an integration test for KV eviction rate under short-batch synthetic loads.
Maria: Also add a performance CI job that runs short-seq and reports memcpy % so we catch this earlier.
Alex: Thanks all — good catch. We'll keep the thread updated. If anyone sees other odd canary signals, ping here. :thumbsup:
